# Chapter 5 · Concatenation: the operand gets escaped, both ways > **Enters as:** `Markup('
')`, with the plain string `'

& '` waiting on the right of the `+` operator The page is finished, and the scenario builds a footer. It writes the literal `Markup("
")`, and the constructor wraps that text without any change ([`__init__.py:122-131`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L122-L131)). Trace line 62 shows the call, and line 63 shows the result, `Markup('
')`. The author controls this literal, so the unguarded constructor from chapter 1 is correct here. The next operand is different. It is the plain string `'

& '`, and it contains a closing paragraph tag, an ampersand, and a script tag. `Markup.__add__` receives that operand as `value` ([`__init__.py:136-140`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L136-L140)). The method first tests `isinstance(value, str) or hasattr(value, "__html__")` ([`__init__.py:137`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L137)). The plain string passes the first test. The method then calls `self.escape(value)` before it joins the 2 strings ([`__init__.py:138`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L138)). Trace line 65 records `Markup.escape(cls=Markup, s='

& ')`. The operand now walks the road of chapter 1. `Markup.escape` calls the module-level `escape` ([`__init__.py:235`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L235)). `escape` sees an exact `str`, so it takes the fast path and calls `_escape_inner` ([`__init__.py:39-40`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L39-L40)). The 5 characters change, and the trace shows the result at line 68: `Markup('</p> & <script>oops</script>')`. `super().__add__` then joins the 2 texts, and `self.__class__(...)` wraps the joined text ([`__init__.py:138`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L138)). Trace lines 71 to 73 show the new value, `Markup('
</p> & <script>oops</script>')`. > **For the owner:** This operator carries the main guarantee for everyday code. Safe markup plus untrusted text gives safe markup, because `__add__` escapes the right operand every time. `Markup.__radd__` does the same work for the other direction, and escapes the left operand first ([`__init__.py:142-146`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L142-L146)). The order of the operands does not change the result. The second `+` has a `Markup` on the right. `Markup("
")` is built at trace line 74, and `__add__` runs again at line 76. The guard accepts the value, and `Markup.escape` runs again at line 77. This time `escape` sees a `Markup`, so `type(s) is str` is false and the `__html__` branch wins ([`__init__.py:42-43`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L42-L43)). `Markup.__html__` returns `self` ([`__init__.py:133-134`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L133-L134)), so `
` stays a live tag. Trace line 88 shows the complete footer, `Markup('
</p> & <script>oops</script>
')`. The scenario printed it through `Markup.__repr__` at line 90 ([`__init__.py:167-168`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L167-L168)). One road stays unused in this run. An operand that is not a `str` and has no `__html__` makes `__add__` return `NotImplemented` ([`__init__.py:140`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L140)). Python then raises `TypeError`. An integer added to a `Markup` fails loudly, and the library does not convert it to text in silence. The same pattern covers the rest of the `str` methods on `Markup`. `join` escapes every element of the iterable ([`__init__.py:170-171`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L170-L171)). `replace` escapes only its `new` argument ([`__init__.py:257-258`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L257-L258)). `ljust`, `rjust` and `center` escape the fill character ([`__init__.py:260-264`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L260-L264), [`__init__.py:272-273`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L272-L273)). `strip`, `lstrip`, `rstrip`, `removeprefix`, `removesuffix` and `partition` do not escape their arguments ([`__init__.py:266-276`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L266-L276), [`__init__.py:297-311`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L297-L311)). Version 3.0.0 made that difference on purpose, because these methods search text and do not insert text ([`CHANGES.rst:55-60`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/CHANGES.rst#L55-L60)). > **For the owner:** Caution: the slice methods keep the type but can break the text. `__getitem__`, `split`, `rsplit` and `splitlines` return `Markup` pieces ([`__init__.py:242-243`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L242-L243), [`__init__.py:173-186`](https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/blob/b2e4d9c7687be25695fffbe93a37622302b24fb1/src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L173-L186)). A slice can cut an entity such as `&` in half. The result is still typed as safe, but the markup is malformed. Check any code that truncates a `Markup` for display, for example a preview or a summary. > **Leaves as:** `Markup('
</p> & <script>oops</script>
')` ```python proof import os import sys sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("src")) from markupsafe import Markup, escape class User: def __init__(self, id, name): self.id = id self.name = name def __html_format__(self, format_spec): if format_spec == "link": return Markup('{}').format(self.id, self.__html__()) elif format_spec: raise ValueError("Invalid format spec") return self.__html__() def __html__(self): return Markup('{0}').format(self.name) # Chapters 1 to 4, replayed. untrusted_comment = "" safe_comment = escape(untrusted_comment) assert safe_comment == "<script>alert(document.cookie);</script>" assert escape(safe_comment) is not None and escape(safe_comment) == safe_comment user = User(3, 'Alice "The Great"') template = Markup("

User: {user:link} said: {comment}

") page = template.format(user=user, comment=safe_comment) assert page == ( '

User: ' "Alice "The <b>Great</b>"" " said: <script>alert(document.cookie);</script>

" ) # Chapter 5, step by step. opening = Markup("
") assert type(opening) is Markup assert str(opening) == "
" # Trace line 65 to 70: the plain operand is escaped. assert Markup.escape("

& ") == ( "</p> & <script>oops</script>" ) # Trace line 64 to 73: safe + untrusted. partial = opening + "

& " assert type(partial) is Markup assert str(partial) == "
</p> & <script>oops</script>" # Trace line 77 to 86: a Markup operand passes through unchanged. assert str(Markup.escape(Markup("
"))) == "
" # Trace line 76 to 89: safe + safe, with no second escape. footer = partial + Markup("
") assert type(footer) is Markup assert str(footer) == ( "
</p> & <script>oops</script>
" ) # Trace line 90 to 91: repr names the class. assert repr(footer) == ( "Markup('
</p> & <script>oops</script>
')" ) # The road not taken: a non-str operand without __html__ raises TypeError. try: Markup("
") + 42 except TypeError: pass else: raise AssertionError("expected TypeError") print("chapter 5 verified") ```
